rows.evidence: Q1: Section 4 (System Application and Verification) and Table 2 <U+2014> the authors deployed their ZigBee/fuzzy controller on three drip-irrigated plots in Mahoba District, UP, measured communication bit error rate at 250 m node distance (<2.2%) and recorded 40 sets of weather readings with valve-opening percentages from March to September 2023.
rows.notes: The study is a primary system-design paper with a small field deployment. On water saving it only states, in Section 4, that the outcome of the system 'claims to save 10% water' compared to a traditional system; no water-application measurements, no comparison treatment and no calculation are reported. Table 2 reports valve opening percentages versus temperature/humidity/pressure/wind, not water volumes. The authors' own evidence covers communication reliability and valve control behaviour, not a quantified water-saving effect, so Q2 is answered 'no' under the when-in-doubt rule. Note also that the review attributes a central value near 40% to this study, whereas the study's only figure is 10%. No dispersion measures, no site/crop replication (one farm, three plots, one district), no stated conditions or limitations on the water-saving claim (the only limitation stated concerns star-topology energy consumption).

notes: Full text appears complete (conference proceeding, 12 pages). The system is described as a sprinkler controller but was field-tested on a drip system; this does not affect the rating since the claim concerns sensor-based smart irrigation control generally.
